text: **Mutation completeness (D32): every state an entity can enter, it can leave, by a service call reachable from every surface.** No state transition exists only as a hand-edit. Held to a mechanical test rather than a review: for each modelled state field, the set of transitions offered by the service layer is closed -- an entity that can be moved into a state and not out of it fails, naming the state and the missing inverse. Ruled by hv 2026-08-15 on a concrete instance vc hit while using the apparatus: `intent ac satisfy` is a one-way door, `rescope`/`reinstate` only undo a descope, so a verifier whose evidence proved incomplete had to hand-edit `acceptance.md` -- the file the CLI exists to own -- to reopen an AC. **A state that can be entered and not left is a missing mutation, not a missing flag.** In WP-04 because `ac`/`at` are its families; the same rule binds D30's whiteboard operations and anything else that models state. **STRENGTHENED AGAIN 2026-08-15 once hv ratified the three state machines (`data-model.md`, State machines): the implemented graph must MATCH THE RATIFIED MACHINES EXACTLY -- no undeclared edge, no missing declared edge, no undeclared state.** Closure is now the weaker half of this: a graph can be closed and still be the wrong graph. This changes the walk's question from _is the code closed?_ to _does the code implement the ratified machine?_, and it turns every verb the machines require -- `st triage`, `st hold`, `st resume`, `st reopen`, `st reinstate`, `wp reopen`, `wp unstart` -- from prose into a red test until it exists. **Evidence that this was needed rather than tidy: `wp done` had no inverse, so two WPs reopened in the contract kept reporting `Done` while their own gate said BLOCKED, and a third reported `WIP` on a PASSING gate -- three of five units disagreeing with themselves, in this thread, caused by the verifier.** **STRENGTHENED 2026-08-15 on cc's own mutation finding, because the clause above is necessary and NOT sufficient and was proven so against the ruled defect itself**: with scope changes clearing satisfaction, deleting `ac.unsatisfy` left `satisfied: true` formally leavable via descope-then-rescope, so the closure walk went green over the exact one-way door hv ruled on. The exit was real and useless -- withdrawing a claim of evidence would mean moving the requirement to another thread and bringing it back, recording two false facts to undo one true one. **The sufficient form: a state you can only leave by changing a DIFFERENT field is still a state you cannot leave.** Edges are therefore classified Direct or Incidental; an incidental edge counts for reachability and NEVER discharges a trap. Noted because it generalises: cc's own correct fix is what disarmed the test for the defect it was written against. **SECOND CONDITION, vc 2026-08-15: a field declared `Unbuilt` discharges this AC only if an entity cannot HOLD a non-initial value of it by any path, ingest included -- not merely if it carries no declared edges.** A field settable at creation or arriving by ingest has been entered, and an entity sitting in a state no service call can leave fails this AC whether or not the disposition table says the work is owed elsewhere. Asserting that the `Unbuilt` rows name a WP and carry no edges checks the BOOKKEEPING and not the property, which is the same shape as the mutation above -- a check right about the set it looked at, looking at the wrong set
